title: Ledger records
description: The append-only records written by the ledger store. Exactly one `call_terminal` record exists per attempted call (R3); the other record kinds carry the lineage the aggregate needs to attribute that call to a root. Every record is append-only and never rewritten.

lineage.description: The lineage vector on a call record. `root_id` is inherited from process context and never supplied by the caller (R1); there is deliberately no way to assert a root in this structure other than the one the registry resolved.

attempt.description: Distinguishes a caller-issued retry from the first call. R3 requires retries to be separate rows rather than collapsed into one.

status.description: `incomplete` and `cancelled` are non-ok terminal states that the aggregate fails closed on (R15). A call that never reached the provider is still `failed` and still gets a row (R3, R6).

served_from.description: A replay row must never be summed into a scored aggregate (R15).

usage_source.description: Where the usage numbers came from. `unknown` with a null usage block is the honest state when the provider reported nothing; it is not a zero.

price_table_id.description: Identity of the versioned price table that produced estimated_usd, recorded per row so a later rate change cannot retroactively re-price history (KTD7).

provider_reported_usd.description: The provider's own cost figure when it reports one. Retained beside the computed figure so the arithmetic has an external check rather than certifying itself.

estimated_usd.description: Cost computed from price_table_id. This is the billed_usd-versus-estimated_usd naming convention: a bare `cost` field would silently answer two different questions.
